errors.text: The critical threshold is placed between 600 and 750 K, whereas the target mechanism shifts at approximately 900 K; behavior remains comparatively stable through 600 K.
The proposed increase and proliferation of dislocations and stacking faults contradicts the target trend of a significant reduction in dislocation density at 900–1200 K.

The hypothesis treats stacking-fault coalescence and amorphization as the primary high-temperature mechanism, while the target describes a shift away from stacking-fault-mediated plasticity toward rapid lattice disorder and softening.
It predicts a direct modulus decline above the inferred 600 K threshold, missing the modulus increase from about 173 GPa at 300 K to 219 GPa at 600 K before the subsequent decline.
